fields.scenarioBasis: A ransomware event removes the EHR for 24 hours. Chosen because cyber disruption ranks highest in the hazard vulnerability analysis and the plan has not been tested for clinical systems.
fields.participants: CIO, CMIO, CNIO, nursing supervisors, laboratory, pharmacy, HIM, security, privacy

areas.finding: The downtime declaration reached units by overhead page but not by email; two units learned it 40 minutes late.
areas.action: Add the downtime page to the paging script. Owner: IT operations. Due 12/15.

areas.finding: Back-entry staffing was not planned; units pulled nurses from the bedside.
areas.action: Name back-entry teams in the downtime plan. Owner: CNIO. Due 01/15.

areas.finding: Players could not say which results to trust after the interface returned.
areas.action: Write a result validation rule for recovery. Owner: CMIO. Due 12/15.

areas.finding: Badge access to the downtime command post was not tested.
areas.action: Test access at the next drill. Owner: Security. Due 12/01.

areas.finding: Label stock for downtime registration lasts about 6 hours.
areas.action: Raise par level on each unit. Owner: Materials. Due 11/30.

areas.finding: Generator coverage for the downtime printers was not confirmed.
areas.action: Confirm and label emergency outlets. Owner: Facilities. Due 12/01.

planRevisions: Emergency operations plan, section on clinical system downtime: add restore order and validation rule.
Communications plan: add the downtime page.
